neighbours.label: a warning or ultimatum as a threat of consequences ('after being warned', 'issued an ultimatum')
fire: Drivers lose their licence if they speed again after being warned.
The landlord gave the tenants an ultimatum: pay or leave within a week.
Players who swear after being warned are sent off the field.
The rebels ignored the army's final ultimatum and stayed in the city.
He was warned twice before the company finally fired him.
Parents should avoid an ultimatum, since a teenager may treat it as a dare.
Shops that keep selling after being warned face heavy fines.
The minister delivered an ultimatum to the strikers on Friday.
quiet: Drivers lose their way if they turn again after being lost.
The landlord gave the tenants a calendar: blue with a picture of a lake.
Players who score after being substituted are cheered off the field.
The rebels visited the army's old museum and stayed in the city.
He was promoted twice before the company finally moved him.
Parents should buy a helmet, since a teenager may ride to school.
Shops that keep selling after being closed earn extra tips.
The minister delivered a speech to the students on Friday.
